column1: # GE-T10's synonym set: a subject the question names by a name the store does not write at all.
# WHY. Spelled, stemmed, derived and surname passes (rules 22 to 25, 29, 33) find a subject only
# when some form of its written name is in the question. A question that calls smallpox the
# Blattern, scurvy the Scharbock, or Semmelweis the saviour of mothers names nothing any of them
# can reach; nor does one that asks after miasma as bad air in another language. Every synonym
# below was checked against `fixtures/dossier/gold/corpus.smy` before it was written: none is an
# entity's name, and none but *epidemiology* and *antiseptic* (inside the epithets for Snow and
# Lister) is anywhere in its text.
# THE RULE, DECLARED before a word of this set was written; scored first without it
# (`baseline.txt`), and not changed after a run:
#  34. a subject by meaning: when no pass finds any run, the question's topic, whole, is put to
#      the store's semantic source, and each entity is scored by the best cosine of its own unit
#      or of any unit that mentions it (`x.text/mentions`). The best entity names the subject
#      when its score is at least T; when the second-best is within M of it, SMY-W417, as any
#      two candidates are. No semantic source, no pass: it finds nothing, as the other passes'
#      defaults do. Last, behind rule 33, so that no question an earlier pass reads changes. A
#      dossier whose subject this pass found records the model's hash; one any other pass
#      found does not, and stays model-free.
#      T and M are fixed on `calibrate.tsv`, written with this file and disjoint from it, before
#      this file is scored with the rule, and are not changed after.
# THE SET. Columns: qid, subject, lang, question — as the surname set. `subject` is the entity
# label the question is about, or `none` for a question that names nobody the store writes and
# should find no subject. The `gd-` rows are the guards: a disease, a substance and two men the
# corpus does not hold as subjects, each near one it does — measles beside smallpox, caloric
# beside phlogiston, malaria (*bad air*) beside miasma, Pasteur and Koch beside Lister, the
# father of microbiology beside the fathers of immunology and epidemiology, and the plague,
# which the corpus mentions without making it a subject.
# Each question's intent was checked to read (`dossier::classify`) before the baseline was
# taken, and a wording that did not read was changed then: the rule under test is the subject's,
# and an unread question never asks for one.
# WHO WROTE THIS. The hand that declared the rule, after declaring it. Single hand.
